prompt: If one wanted to create a data quality application that runs on data stored in HDFS, what would be a good way to approach this? Specifically, assuming the user has defined data quality rules, what would be a good way to evaluate them (specifically in terms of performance)?
response: To create a data quality application for data stored in HDFS, you can use a MapReduce job to evaluate data quality rules. The mapper can read data from HDFS, apply the rules, and output the results. The reducer can then aggregate the results to provide an overall data quality report. This approach is simple and leverages Hadoop's distributed processing capabilities.
